comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming operating income decreased to $290 million in 2024 from $971 million in 2023, primarily driven by lower revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose performance metrics for their Gaming segments in Item 7. NVDA reports Gaming revenue growth of 15% driven by channel inventory normalization, whereas AMD reports a significant decline in Gaming operating income to $290 million from $971 million, primarily driven by lower revenue. While both peers operate in the same gaming hardware market, their financial outcomes in fiscal 2024 diverged sharply: NVDA saw growth due to inventory normalization, while AMD faced substantial operating income contraction due to lower revenue.

sentences.text: Graphics revenue - The year-on-year increase was led by growth in Gaming of 15% driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels.
Gaming operating income was $290 million in 2024, compared to operating income of $971 million in 2023.
The decrease in operating income was primarily driven by lower revenue.
